key_insight: A competitive generative model can be built with a minimalist single-step design using IMLE and a convolutional network, without iterative denoising.
engineering_relevance: This suggests simpler, parameter-efficient generative pipelines may achieve strong sample quality and faster generation for practical deployment.
method: Train with Implicit Maximum Likelihood Estimation (IMLE).
Use a moderately sized convolutional network instead of a transformer.
Add only essential components, avoiding variational inference, adversarial training, and numerical integration.
evidence_signal: On ImageNet 256, the model reports FID 2.56 and also achieves good precision and recall.
watch_item: The abstract highlights strong ImageNet results, but real-world robustness and scalability beyond the reported benchmark should be validated before adoption.
paper_title: ROMS-IMLE: A Minimalist Approach to Competitive Single-Step Generative Modelling
